summary: The study demonstrates a defect mitigation strategy for area-selective deposition (ASD) of ruthenium on TiN/SiO2 nanopatterns using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process exploits the size-dependent reactivity of Ru nanoparticles to suppress defect growth, allowing for the etching of defects while preserving the integrity of the selectively grown film. The ALD temperature is adjusted to control particle growth and enhance selectivity, with the process validated using self-focusing secondary ion mass spectrometry (SF-SIMS). The approach enables defect-free ASD for nanoscale patterning applications.
